description: base + models examples (7 files). Demonstrate base content/error types and the models token-counting, cost, and three proposed-interface model capabilities. Independent of the other FEATs except that all FEATs share one worktree and run sequentially. Read .agents/tasks/example-coverage/context.json and this file FIRST; the full per-file Digest with exact signatures is in .agents/tasks/example-coverage/plan.md.
steps: Create examples/base/content_chunks.py (Live). Build and inspect ContentChunk(text, metadata={}, chunk_id=None, source=None) from skye.base.messages (str(chunk)->text) and StreamChunk(id, delta, finish_reason=None, index=0) from skye.base.completion; show accumulating a few StreamChunk deltas into a final string. No client needed. main() + if __name__ guard.

Create examples/base/errors.py (Live). Import from skye.base.exceptions and raise+catch each: SkyeError(message, details=None), ProviderError(message, provider, status_code=None), ConfigurationError(message), ValidationError(message, field, value), CapabilityExecutionError(message, capability_name); catch SkyeError as the umbrella. Also raise MissingExtraError('postgres', 'asyncpg') and print its message. Print these as normal informative lines — do NOT include any FAILURE_MARKER substring (no 'ValidationError:' etc. literally printed on a normal line, and no 'Traceback').

Create examples/models/token_counting.py (Live). Use skye.models TokenCounter.count_tokens(text, model) and count_message_tokens([UserMessage(...)], model). Note in the docstring that exact counts need the openai extra (tiktoken, absent offline) and that the stdlib approximate path is what runs here; print the approximate numbers.

Create examples/models/cost_tracking.py (Live). Use CostCalculator.calculate_cost(model, usage), add_custom_pricing(model, prompt, completion), get_pricing(model). Create client = skye.provider('openai', api_key=os.environ.get('OPENAI_API_KEY')) (guard-return if unset), do one complete(), and compute the per-request cost from response.usage (TokenUsage).

Create examples/models/cohere.py (proposed-interface, guarded). Top docstring: cohere is registered today only as an embedding provider, not a language model provider; this shows the intended skye.provider('cohere') completion call. Guard by checking skye.models.ProviderRegistry for a cohere MODEL provider; if absent, print a short 'not yet implemented in src' note and return. Do not invent a completion result.

Create examples/models/decision_model.py (proposed-interface, guarded). Import DecisionModel and DecisionResult from skye.base.interfaces.decision. Define a tiny local class implementing the Port (async decide(prompt, options)->DecisionResult) to show the call shape (choice + probabilities summing to 1.0, reject empty options with a Skye error). Docstring notes no concrete decision model ships in src yet. Run it with asyncio.run.

Create examples/models/retry_and_errors.py (proposed-interface, guarded). Show catching a real skye.base.exceptions.ProviderError and the SkyeError hierarchy, and explain that transient-error retry is configured at the router level (reference examples/routing). Do not fake a retry switch. Any intentionally shown error line must contain the word 'Expected'.
Run uv run black on the new files and fix any ruff findings (sorted imports, remove unused imports) so both are clean on examples/base and examples/models.
acceptance_criteria: uv run pytest tests/examples -q -k 'base or models' passes (new files discovered and green)
uv run ruff check examples/base examples/models reports no errors
uv run black --check examples/base examples/models reports nothing to reformat
No new file prints a FAILURE_MARKER on a normal path; any deliberate error line contains 'Expected'
No pydantic used for any user-facing shape; no top-level import of a forbidden-at-import library
verification: uv run pytest tests/examples -q -k 'base or models'
uv run ruff check examples/base examples/models
findings: Created 7 files. Live (run real library code): base/content_chunks.py (ContentChunk/StreamChunk), base/errors.py (full SkyeError hierarchy + MissingExtraError), models/token_counting.py (TokenCounter approximate path; tiktoken absent offline), models/cost_tracking.py (skye.provider('openai').complete() then CostCalculator on response.usage). Proposed-interface, guarded: models/cohere.py (guards on ProviderRegistry.list_model_providers() lacking cohere, which is embedding-only), models/decision_model.py (local FirstOptionDecider implementing the DecisionModel Port, run via asyncio.run, rejects empty options with ValidationError shown as an 'Expected' line), models/retry_and_errors.py (real ProviderError + SkyeError umbrella; notes retry is router-level, references examples/routing). Notes for later FEATs: (1) FAILURE_MARKER avoidance works even though SkyeError.__init__ calls logger.error with 'ProviderError:'-style text; the default logging lastResort handler output is NOT captured by capsys, so those log lines do not trip the harness. Still, never print a bare 'ErrorName: message' on a normal stdout line. (2) Any deliberately-provoked error line must contain the word 'Expected'. (3) README.md was NOT touched (that is FEAT step 11 / a later FEAT); add a base and models category entry there. (4) House style followed quickstart.py: module docstring, def main()/async main + asyncio.run, early return with printed skip note, if __name__ guard. Verification on new paths only (whole-tree ruff/black fail on pre-existing out-of-scope files, left untouched).
